title: People’s Mañanera July 30
author: Pedro Gellert
content:
_Every day, President Claudia Sheinbaum gives a morning presidential press
conference and Mexico Solidarity Media posts English language summaries,
translated by Mexico Solidarity 's Pedro Gellert. Previous press conference
summaries are available [here](https://mexicosolidarity.com/mananera/)._

**Mañanera Presidential Press Conference: Speaking to the People Without
Intermediaries  
** President Claudia Sheinbaum defended the Morning Press Conference, known as
the mañanera, as a space to directly inform the public, display
accountability, and exercise the right of reply. “When have we censored the
media? It's one thing that we disagree with what they publish and we exercise
the right of reply here, and quite another what was done in the past,” she
explained. Sheinbaum maintained that “there has never been more freedom of
expression as there is now.”

**Political Debate Must Be Based on Truth  
** The President welcomed the National Electoral Institute’s (INE) order for
the PRI to withdraw its materials that tied Morena to drug trafficking,
deeming them slanderous. “That’s good, because the INE has the responsibility
to ensure that political disputes are truthful, that there is no use of fake
news or baseless arguments, and that the debate is constructive, not
aggressive,” Sheinbaum stated.

**The Economy Maintains Its Momentum  
** Sheinbaum characterized as “very good news” the quarterly GDP growth of
1.5% (2.5% in annual terms), driven by the agricultural and services sectors,
while manufacturing halted its decline. The President anticipated that the
second half of the year will be better thanks to public work projects, the
Housing for Wellbeing program, and government investment.

**Strengthening the Strategy Against Sargassum  
** The President announced an investment of more than 2 billion pesos (US$110
million) to strengthen efforts to reduce sargassum in Quintana Roo with boats,
barriers, and monitoring. “The state government has done a great deal, but we
have to do more,” Sheinbaum said. In addition, a circular economy is being
promoted with 190 initiatives, 39 companies, and the development of
biofertilizers, biogas, and other derivative products.

**Education Must Be a Space of Freedom  
** The President supported the closure of militarized schools following the
death of student Dafne Quintos and said that “under the pretext of discipline
there are abuses, and that cannot be allowed.” She reaffirmed that education
must be a space of freedom and the building of freedom.

**Mexico Maintains Its Solidarity With Cuba  
** Sheinbaum rejected the use of Mexico by U.S. politicians for electoral
purposes: “Mexico is no one’s piñata.” She reaffirmed that support for Cuba
will continue for reasons of sovereignty, humanitarian aid, and the self-
determination of peoples, and reiterated Mexico’s rejection of Washington’s
blockade against the island.

**The Defense of Migrants Must Unite the Country  
** The President regretted that the opposition refused to support a statement
in defense of Mexicans in the United States and charged that it “is part of
(their) hypocrisy.” Sheinbaum argued that protecting migrants must be a cause
embraced by all political forces, above partisan interests.
